title: DNA → Chromosome → Gene
guideCell: 1) Look at the whole cell · 2) Zoom in step by step · 3) Find the gene hiding inside the DNA
guideNucleus: The nucleus is the cell's control room — every chromosome lives inside it.
guideChromosome: A chromosome is DNA wound tightly around proteins so it fits inside the nucleus.
guideHelix: Two DNA strands twist together like a spiral staircase, held by base-pair "steps."
guideGene: A gene is just one useful stretch of that DNA — like one sentence in a very long book.
guideTourComplete: Tour complete! Cell → Nucleus → Chromosome → DNA → Gene. Try the quiz below.
helixHint: Twist speed and base pairs apply once you reach the DNA helix.
cellHint: Membrane and organelles show at the whole-cell level.
learnMore: Cell → nucleus → chromosome → DNA → gene: each level lives inside the one before it.
quizQuestion: Where is a gene actually found?
quizCorrect: A segment of DNA inside a chromosome
quizWrong: A separate organelle in the cytoplasm
